title: The Psychology of Money
author: Morgan Housel
takeaway: Wealth is what you don't see. The behavior gap costs more than the fee gap ever will.

title: The Intelligent Investor
author: Benjamin Graham
takeaway: Price is what you pay, value is what you get. Chapter 8 and 20 are the whole book: Mr. Market and margin of safety.

title: Chip War
author: Chris Miller
takeaway: Semiconductors are the new oil. Export controls, fabs, and lithography are geopolitics now — which is exactly why the hardware sleeve exists.

title: The Innovator's Dilemma
author: Clayton Christensen
takeaway: Great companies fail by doing everything right for their existing customers. Watch where the cheap, 'worse' technology is improving fastest.

title: Poor Charlie's Almanack
author: Charlie Munger
takeaway: Invert, always invert. A latticework of mental models beats a single lens.

title: The Price of Time
author: Edward Chancellor
takeaway: A history of interest rates — the backdrop for why the 10-year yield shows up on this site at all.

title: Energy and Civilization
author: Vaclav Smil
takeaway: Every economic era is an energy era first. Compute is no exception.

title: When Genius Failed
author: Roger Lowenstein
takeaway: Two Nobel laureates, a model that had never been wrong, and leverage of 25 to 1. One correlation spike and the Fed had to convene the banks on a Sunday. Models are not the risk; what you borrow against them is.

title: Manias, Panics, and Crashes
author: Charles Kindleberger
takeaway: Every bubble has the same anatomy: displacement, credit, euphoria, distress, panic. Learn the sequence and you stop asking whether this time is different.

title: This Time Is Different
author: Carmen Reinhart and Kenneth Rogoff
takeaway: Eight centuries of sovereign defaults and banking crises in tables. The four most expensive words in finance are the title.

title: The Big Short
author: Michael Lewis
takeaway: 2008 told by the handful who looked at the loans. The system did not fail to see it; it paid everyone not to look.

title: Too Big to Fail
author: Andrew Ross Sorkin
takeaway: The collapse weekend by weekend, from inside the rooms. Who gets saved is decided by phone calls, not rules.

title: Lords of Finance
author: Liaquat Ahamed
takeaway: Four central bankers and the gold standard turned a crash into the Depression. Rates are policy, and policy is people.

title: The Great Crash 1929
author: John Kenneth Galbraith
takeaway: Short and funny about the least funny year in markets. The bezzle: the stock of undiscovered embezzlement that grows in good times and surfaces in bad.

title: Devil Take the Hindmost
author: Edward Chancellor
takeaway: A history of speculation from tulips forward. The instruments change; the crowd does not.

title: A Demon of Our Own Design
author: Richard Bookstaber
takeaway: Crashes come from complexity and tight coupling, not from stupidity. The hedge everyone shares becomes the thing it was hedging against; 1987 in one sentence.

title: Crashed
author: Adam Tooze
takeaway: 2008 was a global dollar-funding crisis, not an American housing story, and the ten years after it were the response. The longest and the most complete account.

title: The Black Swan
author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
takeaway: Fat tails and survivorship. You can be right for twenty years and ruined in a day, and the twenty years taught you nothing about the day.

title: Debt: The First 5,000 Years
author: David Graeber
takeaway: Debt as a moral and political technology older than money. The darkest frame on the shelf, and the one that explains the most.

title: The Smartest Guys in the Room
author: Bethany McLean and Peter Elkind
takeaway: Enron. A room full of smart people and no number anyone could check. The scoreboard was marked to a model, and that is the whole lesson.

title: Capital in the Twenty-First Century
author: Thomas Piketty
takeaway: r > g: capital compounds faster than wages. A grievance if all you have is labor, a strategy the day you own some r.
